name: Saint Bartholomew, Apostle
vocation: Apostle and witness to Jesus Christ
briefBio: Bartholomew is named in the Synoptic Gospel lists of the Twelve and among the apostles gathered in Acts. The New Testament gives no further secure biography. Identifying him with Nathanael in John's Gospel is an ancient and widely received interpretation, not an explicit scriptural statement. Eusebius later reports a tradition connecting Bartholomew with a Gospel found in India; Armenian missions, martyrdom places and methods, and relic journeys belong to diverse later receptions. His feast therefore centers faithful apostolic companionship and Christ's mission without inventing dates, graphic death scenes, or national ownership.

editorial.reviewer: Catholic Daily factual and theological review

whyItMatters: Bartholomew shows that faithful discipleship does not need an embellished biography. A small canonical footprint can still call us to remain with Christ, serve in community, and handle beloved traditions with honesty and peace.
oneMinuteSummary: Bartholomew is named among the Twelve in the Synoptic Gospels and among the apostles gathered after Jesus' Ascension. Scripture supplies no birth, death, travel, or writing record for him. The familiar identification with Nathanael in John's Gospel is an ancient and widely received interpretation based partly on his association with Philip, but the text never states it. Eusebius, writing centuries later, reports a tradition linking Bartholomew to a Gospel encountered in India. Claims about Armenia, exact routes, relic transfers, and martyrdom by beheading, crucifixion, or skinning come from varied later traditions and cannot be merged into one eyewitness biography. His feast can therefore honor apostolic companionship, mission, and perseverance without graphic spectacle, dangerous imitation, or nationalist ownership. Faithful memory welcomes tradition while keeping Scripture and historical claims distinct.

sections.heading: Named among the apostles
sections.body: Matthew names Bartholomew among the Twelve, and Acts places him in the gathered apostolic community. These texts establish belonging and mission, not a detailed later biography.

sections.heading: Bartholomew and Nathanael
sections.body: Many Christians identify Bartholomew with Nathanael, partly because Philip accompanies each name in different Gospel patterns. Ancient evidence also contains alternatives, so the identification remains received interpretation rather than explicit Scripture.

sections.heading: India and Armenia traditions
sections.body: Eusebius reports that Pantaenus encountered an India tradition associated with Bartholomew. Armenian and other mission claims developed in later reception; they deserve respectful study without becoming certain routes or national possession.

sections.heading: Divergent martyr memories
sections.body: Later sources disagree about place and method of death. Graphic skinning imagery and relic narratives are not the secure historical core, and martyr witness never requires seeking violence or neglecting safety.

life.gospelTheme: Christ calls disciples by name into a shared mission whose truth does not depend on later fame or elaborate legend.
life.struggle: Sparse canonical evidence invited later traditions to supply identity, journeys, relics, and violent deaths with more certainty than the sources allow.
life.response: Stay close to Christ and the apostolic community, receive traditions gratefully but critically, and reject violence, spectacle, or national ownership as measures of faith.

virtues.name: Faithful presence
virtues.evidence: The canonical record remembers Bartholomew as one of the Twelve and as part of the gathered apostolic community.
virtues.imitation: Keep one quiet commitment to your worshiping or serving community without needing recognition.

virtues.name: Truthful humility
virtues.evidence: Early and later sources preserve meaningful reception while leaving identity, itinerary, and martyrdom questions unresolved.
virtues.imitation: When sharing a religious story, name clearly what Scripture says, what tradition receives, and what remains uncertain.

practice.spiritual: Read Matthew 10:1–8 slowly and receive discipleship as a shared call from Christ, not a contest for dramatic stories.
practice.action: Correct one embellished claim you have repeated, preserving what is spiritually meaningful while naming its source and level of certainty.

reflectionQuestions: Can I remain faithful when my service is ordinary and largely unseen?
Do I distinguish Scripture, early reception, and later legend without contempt for any of them?

scripture.connection: Bartholomew appears within a community called and sent by Jesus, centering his feast on received mission rather than unsupported biography.

prayer: Lord Jesus, who called Bartholomew among the apostles, keep us faithful in community, humble before the evidence, courageous without seeking danger, and ready to serve without spectacle or possession. Amen.
